//: Markdown lint rules. Read before adding a rule: super-linter runs this across every Markdown file, so a newly enabled rule fails CI on pre-existing content. Enable a rule only alongside a cleanup pass over the files it flags.
//_frontmatter: MD025 is disabled because markdownlint counts the YAML frontmatter block as a title, so every file in this repo reports a false 'multiple H1'. The hub requires exactly one H1, and check_frontmatter.py enforces that the H1 follows the frontmatter.
//_line_length: Prose is hard-wrapped by hand. Enforcing a column limit would fight the existing writing style and produce diff noise on every wrapped sentence.
//_tables: MD060 is disabled because the hub uses compact table pipes (|-----|-----|) throughout for density. This is a deliberate style choice, not an oversight.
//_code_fences: MD040 is disabled because many fences are illustrative output (console, file trees, raw DAX results) where a language identifier adds nothing. Fences that are actually runnable should still carry a language.
//_bare_urls: MD034 is disabled because governance and access-control docs contain illustrative bare email addresses in tables. Autofixing them to <angle-bracket> autolinks changes the visible cell text, which is worse than the lint finding in a reference table.
//_emphasis_headings: MD036 is disabled because several documents use bold text as a visual label inside longer sections.
//_html: MD033 is disabled because some documents embed HTML anchors for cross-referencing.
//_first_line_h1: MD041 is disabled because documents begin with frontmatter before their H1, which this rule does not model.
//_code_block_style: MD046 is disabled because documents use both fenced and indented styles for short inline code blocks.
//_duplicate_headings: Sibling-only: repeated '## Examples' under different parents is fine and common here.
